extractedFacts.wrongfulLockoutCitation: Minnesota's enhanced wrongful-lockout remedy (Minn. Stat. Sec. 504B.225/504B.231 -- 3x damages or $500, whichever greater, plus attorney's fees; criminal exposure under Sec. 609.606) is confirmed to apply to RESIDENTIAL tenancies only -- Minnesota Statutes Chapter 504B does not govern purely commercial leases. No confirmed commercial-specific statutory enhancement found.

outcome.description: The district court granted Lagoon summary judgment in June 2022, held the liquidated-damages clause enforceable so that no mitigation was required, and (after Lagoon waived attorney fees) entered judgment for $1,808,470 plus costs. The Minnesota Court of Appeals reversed on December 11, 2023, holding the liquidated-damages clause unenforceable because actual damages were capable of estimation and the clause ignored the duty to mitigate, and remanded for further proceedings on actual damages and mitigation.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed (liquidated-damages clause unenforceable) and remanded; no final figure yet.

Removed: the syllabus and opening paragraph stating the court's conclusion, the block quote of the statutory-limit liquidated-damages language, the executive-order citations, footnotes, the paragraph describing the district court's summary-judgment order and judgment amount, and all analysis.
